products.name: Tesla Optimus
products.note: Humanoid robot; factory automation; physical safety; worker interaction; liability

reading.body:
Tesla's most notable AI product in this dataset is Tesla Optimus, a humanoid robot positioned in the Emerging and Frontier AI category, with noted applications in factory automation and worker interaction alongside concerns about physical safety and liability.

The data covers one product entry and basic corporate identifiers: a founding year of 2003, a Palo Alto headquarters, and a public-company structure. No compute figures, power consumption, data center footprint, or revenue are present, so no claims can be made about Tesla's position in the AI scaling chain from that angle. What the product note does establish is that Optimus moves AI inference into physical space, where the binding constraints shift from grid capacity to mechanical reliability and legal exposure.

Factory automation at scale requires robots to operate continuously in environments shared with human workers, which introduces failure modes that software-only systems do not face. Physical safety and liability appear explicitly in the product note, signaling that deployment friction for this class of AI is regulatory and actuarial as much as it is technical. The data does not cover training infrastructure, energy draw, or manufacturing capacity for Optimus units, so the relationship between this product and compute or power constraints remains outside what can be said here.
